newsitem.title: USA: Retrial for alleged 'Hollywood Madam' postponed.
newsitem.headline: Retrial for alleged 'Hollywood Madam' postponed.

text.p: A retrial for reputed Hollywood madam Heidi Fleiss on charges of running a high-priced call-girl ring was postponed Tuesday so she could finish a drug rehabilitation programme she was ordered to attend.

Fleiss, 30, was convicted in state court in 1994 on three counts of pandering in connection with the call-girl ring and was sentenced to three years in prison. But the conviction was reversed by a state appeals court this year because of jury misconduct.
Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Judith Champagne set Jan. 13 as the new date for the retrial.

Fleiss is due to be sentenced in U.S. District Court Jan. 6 on a federal money laundering and tax evasion conviction related to the money she earned from the prostitution ring. She had been free on $150,000 bail but she was jailed in late September after she admitted using the drug methamphetamine.
On Oct. 1, U.S. District Judge Consuelo Marshall ordered Fleiss into a residential drug rehabilitation centre for 90 days. She is expected to complete the programme by the end of the year.

Fleiss, who was allowed to leave the centre for Tuesday's brief hearing, told reporters she was "very homesick," particularly with Thanksgiving approaching. She said she worked in the center's kitchen and would be spending Thursday cooking turkey for the other 300 residents.
